title: Multiplying a Decimal by a Whole Number

blocks.html: You can add decimals, and you know how multiplying by 10 moves digits. Multiplying a decimal by a whole number is repeated adding of tenths or hundredths.
Think of the decimal as a count of tenths or hundredths. Multiply that count by the whole number, then write the result in the same unit: $4 \times 0.3$ is $4 \times 3$ tenths $= 12$ tenths $= 1.2$.

$4 \times 0.3$ means four groups of 3 tenths. That is 12 tenths. Ten tenths make one whole, so 12 tenths is 1 whole and 2 tenths: $1.2$. Units stay units: tenths times a whole number are still tenths.

blocks.cap: Four groups of 3 tenths fill one whole and 2 more tenths: $4 \times 0.3 = 1.2$.

blocks.title: Hundredths
steps: Estimate: $6 \times 2 = 12$, and $6 \times 2.5 = 15$. The answer is between.

blocks.html: Losing track of the unit and writing $6 \times 2.35 = 141$ or $1.41$. Check with an estimate: $2.35$ is a bit more than 2, so six of them are a bit more than 12.
